### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via searchAll (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8b550f8193962a18091b79b8bc890cd63a91dc67` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7e7e69c86b1942a03ea65c7c2a58ef6706254030` — the merge of head `7e8e4e8aa12129e28635c1f2ade5c552c2b963cc` into base `8b550f8193962a18091b79b8bc890cd63a91dc67`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7e7e69c86b1942a03ea65c7c2a58ef6706254030 && git checkout 7e7e69c86b1942a03ea65c7c2a58ef6706254030
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8b550f8193962a18091b79b8bc890cd63a91dc67 7e8e4e8aa12129e28635c1f2ade5c552c2b963cc && git checkout -B drift-repro 8b550f8193962a18091b79b8bc890cd63a91dc67 && git merge --no-ff 7e8e4e8aa12129e28635c1f2ade5c552c2b963cc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8b550f8193962a18091b79b8bc890cd63a91dc67
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8b550f8193962a18091b79b8bc890cd63a91dc67` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：某个应用包被停用后，全局搜索不再搜出它的记录，跟打开列表、打开详情时的表现一致。
- 为什么做：以前停用后列表和详情都打不开，但全局搜索还能看到这些记录的标题和匹配内容，等于停用没停干净。
- 出错会怎样：最坏情况是停用包的记录仍出现在搜索里，和修之前一样。没有停用任何包的环境完全不受影响；重新启用后就能再次搜到。
- 要你做什么：不需要你做任何事。它收窄了对外接口的返回结果，席位会安排一次约定审核，然后由区域落地。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#5 · head `cc13fef36fce6ee8eed1c69f3c0eb5c848f44df8` · 2026-11-19T07:03Z

- **形态** — 3 files, +212/−0: `metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts` (+17), a new card-named test, and one changeset. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35367`: not governed, under the 3000-line limit. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — an L2 face; see routing below.
- **Fixes vs card #35195** — the `searchAll` sweep now asks `isObjectOfDisabledPackage(registry, obj.name)` beside the exposure decision, before any query. A disabled package's object is therefore never queried, named or counted in `totalObjects`. An explicit `?objects=` naming it reads as one naming no object. `readReferenceTitles` asks the same predicate of a title target, so an enabled hit that points into a disabled package keeps the bare id, the same answer an unreadable target already gets. The helper is the one `protocol-authoring-refusals.ts` already exports, and it optional-calls `registry.isObjectPackageDisabled`, the predicate the data routes and `meta-object-state-routes` ask. A registry that cannot answer hides nothing.
- **Changeset** — read sentence by sentence against the diff. The BREAKING banner, the data-route 404 comparison, "never queried, never named, never counted", the `?objects=` reading, the title-target paragraph, the re-enable fix and "pages already filtered" all match. The ADR-0087 marker is present (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), and its reason holds: no key, value or type moves, and nothing stored is rewritten.
- **Ruling asked: `Metadata-protocol` → `none`** — AGENTS.md defines the line as the change to *what a metadata author can write*. Disabling a package is an install-state operation by an administrator, not authored metadata, and no authored key changes meaning or default here. The moved answer belongs to a runtime door. The precedents for the same family, disabled-package narrowings, all declare `none`: the `resolveItem` / `MetadataFacade` change, the `/auth/me/permissions` change, the engine function reads and the currency-code message (see the `objectql` / `rest` CHANGELOGs). With `none`, the level is **`patch`**: "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". **Change required:** in the changeset, `Metadata-protocol: semantic` → `none` and `minor` → `patch`, and the same in the PR body. Banner, marker and text stay.
- **Pins** — new `protocol.search-disabled-package-35195.test.ts` covers:
  - THE PIN: not queried, named or counted;
  - a context-less in-process call;
  - `objects=` naming it equals naming no object;
  - a disabled title target lends no title;
  - CONTROLs: re-enabled, it is a hit again and the title reads through again; an enabled object's hits are identical with and without the disable; a registry without the predicate hides nothing.
  The dogfood battery is green on this head (os-dev-report 7001651530).
- **门禁** — 53 check-runs on this head: 37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure.
- **接受的偏差** — none.
- **范围外去向** — none found.
- **L2 owed (routing)** — `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` → a contract review at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER before queue. Routed to seat 5, which also confirms the `Metadata-protocol` ruling above.
- **落地条款** — base `81c09477`, main moved K=17 first-parent commits (≥ 15) → merge main and wait for a green re-run. `git merge-tree` against current main is clean, and main has not touched the two source files. Put the merge and the two changeset/PR-body line changes in one push. This ACCEPT carries over to that head if it contains nothing else. After the seat's L2 record, pkg-2 lands.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7e8e4e8aa12129e28635c1f2ade5c552c2b963cc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.search-disabled-package-35195.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-refusals.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-package-addressing.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/package-registry.zod.ts, content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx (all cited, outside the diff: read, not reviewed)

PR #35367 for card #35195. Net diff against `main`: 3 files, +212/−0 (one source file +17, one new test file, one changeset). Read: the card and all 5 comments, the PR body and its 4 comments, the net diff, and the 57 check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of `GET /api/v1/search` / `searchAll` — narrowed, right.** The record sweep skips an object for which `isObjectOfDisabledPackage(registry, obj.name)` is true, right after the `canServeApiOperation(enable, 'search')` decision and before `canReadObject`, `getQueryableFields`, `objectsScanned++` and `engine.find`. So the object is never queried, never named, never counted in `totalObjects`, and the security service is not asked about it. This is what the changeset states.
- **`?objects=` naming a disabled package's object — right.** It falls to the same `continue`, so it answers as a name with no object behind it. No `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` is raised. That is consistent with the door's stated contract in `protocol.ts` ("An explicit `objects=` naming an unreadable object answers exactly as one naming an object that does not exist"); search is a sweep, and the by-name refusal belongs to `assertObjectRegistered`.
- **Reference titles — narrowed, right.** `readReferenceTitles` asks the same predicate of the lookup target before any read, so an enabled hit whose `nameField` points into a disabled package keeps the bare id. The only caller is the sweep; no other title path in `searchAll` reads a second object.
- **Same predicate as the data door — confirmed in the cited code.** `protocol-query-validation.ts` (`assertObjectRegistered`) throws `objectPackageDisabledError` on the same helper; the helper optional-calls `registry.isObjectPackageDisabled`, which resolves the name through `resolveObjectKey` and asks about the OWNING package only. Search and the data routes therefore cannot disagree about which objects a disable hides, including the overlay case (an extension from a disabled package does not take the enabled owner's object out of search, as it does not take it off the data routes).
- **Pages — no change, claim holds.** The page sweep reads `this.getMetaItems({ type: 'page' })`, and `getMetaItems` filters with `isItemOfDisabledPackage` on every layer except `per-package`.
- **Response shape, public exports, schemas — none moved.** No spec file, no exported signature, no generated baseline is in the diff.
- **A registry without the method hides nothing** — the existing optional-call disposition of the helper, pinned by a control. Right for a test double; the real `SchemaRegistry` always answers.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — confirmed. A caller of the search door on an environment with a disabled package gets fewer hits than before; the `!` in the title and the **BREAKING** banner are owed and present.

**Metadata-protocol: `none`, level `patch` — the L1 ruling is CONFIRMED; the claim's `semantic` / `minor` is rejected.** Grounds, checked here and not taken from L1:

- AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3) defines the line as "the change to what a metadata author can write"; `semantic` is "a changed meaning or default"; "all else is `none`".
- No authorable key, value, type or default is in the diff. The search-related authored keys (`enable.searchable`, `enable.apiMethods`, `searchableFields`, `nameField`) keep their meaning for every enabled package.
- The state the guard reads is install state: `enabled` / `status: 'disabled'` live on the installed-package registry record (`packages/spec/src/kernel/package-registry.zod.ts`) and are set through `PATCH /api/v1/packages/:id/disable`, not written in a manifest. Its published meaning ("hidden, refused on the data plane, and its data is kept", `marketplace-handbook.mdx`) does not change; one more door now honours it.
- Precedent in the same family: `66f6638` in the `metadata-protocol` CHANGELOG, "a name only disabled packages hold answers 404 at `_env`", ships `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- Level: "`none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition." The changeset is `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`, carries both declaration lines, the banner, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), whose reason holds: nothing an author writes moves and nothing stored is rewritten. The only moved package is the one named.

**Check Changeset on this head — two check-runs of that name, one red; the gate IS satisfied.** Verified from the runs, not from the area's account:

- Job `135401677731` (workflow run `44477560875`, PR Automation, event `pull_request`): **failure**. Its log: "The metadata-protocol declaration and the changeset level disagree, inside one PR … metadata-protocol line: `Metadata-protocol: semantic`", against the committed changeset already at `patch`. In the same run `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` ran, which `pr-automation.yml` skips on `labeled` / `unlabeled` / `edited`, so this is the code-event (push) run.
- Job `135402106349` (workflow run `44477688867`, same workflow, same head, created about a minute later): **success**. Its log: "LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② `yes (narrowing)` and metadata-protocol `none`, and it introduces no changeset entry graded `minor` or above … metadata-protocol line: `Metadata-protocol: none`". `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` are skipped in this run, so it is a metadata-event run (the body edit).
- Limit of the evidence: the check-run and run objects expose `event=pull_request` for both, not the event action; the push-versus-edit reading is inferred from which sibling jobs ran. It is consistent on every point.
- The red run judged a PR body that no longer exists. The newer run of the same check on the same head judged the body and changeset as they are now and passed; the PR's `mergeable_state` reads `clean`. The red row is stale, not a finding. It stays visible on the head until that run is re-run; nothing in the tree needs to change for it.

All other check-runs on this head: success or skipped, no other failure.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag — `Metadata-protocol` read as `none` against the claim's `semantic`:** answered in ②, `none` / `patch`.
- **Dev flag — `searchAll` docblock in `protocol.ts` has no paragraph for the disabled-package skip (file outside the card's fence):** accepted as N1 below; follow-up, not this head.
- **Dev flag — `$expand` into a disabled package's object (`servesExpansionTarget` judges declared exposure only):** read here: the function is `canServeApiOperation(schema?.enable, …)` and asks nothing about the package. Whether the expansion sub-read is refused further down was not established by reading and is not this card's door. **Escalated to area pkg-2:** measure it through `GET /api/v1/data/:object?$expand=` and file a card if it serves; it is the same class of leak as this card and must not rest on a note.
- **Dev flag — stale test-file citation in `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts`:** polish, outside the diff; a follow-up at the area's discretion.
- **Dev deviation — no model identifier in commit trailers:** correct per AGENTS.md.
- **`open_questions`:** empty in all three os-dev-reports.
- **SQL push-down:** no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the new check is an in-memory registry predicate per object, and it removes reads. The title read keeps its existing single `id $in` batch.
- **Dogfood battery (narrowing arm) — NOT pinned to this head; owed before `--land`, no head change needed.** The battery ran at `cc13fef3` (482 files / 4092 tests passed). This head differs from it by (a) the changeset's two lines (`minor` → `patch`, `semantic` → `none`), which no test reads, and (b) a merge of `main` bringing 89 files, +3116/−309. The PR's two source files are byte-identical between the two heads, so the battery's evidence about the narrowing itself stands. What it does not cover is the merged tree, and CI did not cover it either: on this head the `Dogfood Regression Gate` shard jobs are **skipped** (the row still carries the unexpanded matrix name) and the aggregate row is a vacuous success. The rule is "全量 dogfood 只在终 head 跑一次" (`os-dev.md`) and `--land` refuses a `(narrowing)` PR unless the latest trusted os-dev-report pins the battery to the head; the latest report says "not re-run at 7e8e4e8a". Main's delta touches nothing under `packages/metadata-protocol` and nothing in the registry's package addressing, so the risk is low, but low risk is not the pin. The area re-runs the battery at this head and reports it; that moves no file, so this record keeps covering the head. This is a landing precondition, not a defect of the contract.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing makes the published refusal real; it takes no declared capability away.** The published meaning of a disable on `main` is one sentence: "Disabled has one meaning: the module is hidden, refused on the data plane, and its data is kept" (`content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx`), and the data routes and by-name metadata reads already answer `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`. Nothing in the spec, the `searchAll` contract docblock or the docs declares that search serves a disabled package's records; the sweep served them only because `getAllObjects()` keeps the schema resolvable and the sweep never asked. So this is not a capability narrowed at a consumer; it is the last record door brought under the rule the others enforce. The capability a caller loses is restored by the declared route, re-enabling the package.

Attempts to break it, all in the cited code:

- *A second read path inside `searchAll`.* The record loop has one `engine.find` per swept object and one title read through `readReferenceTitles`; both are guarded. The page sweep goes through `getMetaItems`, already filtered. No third path.
- *Disclosure by count or name.* The guard precedes `objectsScanned++` and every push to `hits`; a skipped object contributes to neither `totalObjects` nor `totalHits` nor `truncated`.
- *Disclosure by an oracle on `objects=`.* A disabled object and a nonexistent one give the same answer, pinned by deep equality. No refusal code distinguishes them on this door. (The data door distinguishes them on purpose; that is its by-name contract, not a leak created here.)
- *Guard order.* It runs before `canReadObject`, so a permission outage or a denying security service cannot change what a disabled object answers.
- *Name resolution drift.* The sweep passes `obj.name` to the registry's own `resolveObjectKey`-based predicate, the one the read path uses, owner-only. An overlay from a disabled package does not hide the object it decorates; same answer as the data routes.
- *Data of a disabled record inside an enabled hit.* The hit's `record` is the enabled object's own row; a lookup column holds the bare id, which the data route for the enabled object also returns. The only borrowed text was the title, now withheld.
- *The pin.* The test drives the real `searchAll` over a registry double for the predicate; both guards were ablated red and restored. The real registry's predicate has its own pins at the data door.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — `searchAll`'s contract docblock in `protocol.ts` enumerates each skip (exposure, read admission) and now omits the disabled-package one; the reasoning sits only at the guard. Accepted deviation on this head (a fix moves the head); follow-up card for the docblock.
- N2 (nit) — the handbook's "Data plane" bullet names the data routes and by-name metadata reads but not search. It is no longer wrong by omission in the harmful direction, and it is a prose face: a follow-up docs line ("global search leaves the module's records out") is welcome, in a docs PR, not required here.
- N3 (nit) — no pin runs the search door over the real `SchemaRegistry` with a really disabled package (the card's own reproduction: disable, then `GET /api/v1/search`). The unit pin plus the registry's own predicate pins cover the logic; a dogfood case would cover the wiring. Follow-up card at the area's discretion.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-35195-search-disabled-package`
Reviewed-by: `isolated-l2-35367`

**VERDICT: PASS**
